findings.message: `show()` returns "" both when the path is absent at a ref and when `git show` itself fails. The release loop reads that "" as "no open items", so a failed read releases. Fix: return None (or raise) when git fails on a path that `ls-tree` listed at the target, or on config.yaml when it exists there, and exit 2. Treat only a genuinely absent path at <base> as empty.
findings.scenario: Take a partial clone (`--filter=blob:none`) run offline, where target's .specclaw/debt.md holds a new `class:security` item. `ls-tree` succeeds because trees are present, but `git show target:.specclaw/debt.md` fails on the missing blob. `open_items("")` returns [], so the output is `0 open item(s), 0 blocking` and the exit is 0. The security debt is released instead of the gate reporting that it could not read.

findings.message: An unknown or misspelt `release_gate.block_on` name is kept as is. Because finding classes are always one of law/security/data-loss/other, that name never matches anything, so a typo silently turns the gate off. The same happens in the second copy, `Config.block_on` in review_core.py, where the fast track then defers every classified blocker to debt. Fix: reject any name outside CLASSES in both copies, with exit 2 in release and a ReviewError in the review run, instead of narrowing the gate.
findings.scenario: Set config `release_gate:\n  block_on: [securty]` and add a debt item `<!-- fp:x class:security -->` in the range. `specclaw-sync release base HEAD` prints `block_on: securty`, `0 blocking` and exits 0. In the review loop, a fast-track `security` blocker exits 0 and goes to debt.md.

findings.message: An item counts as new when its exact line is missing from the same path at <base>. Moving the file therefore re-lists every open item in it as added. Archiving a change, which moves `changes/<c>/` to `changes/archive/<c>/`, is the normal flow. Fix: key items by their `fp:` marker across all list files at base, falling back to the line text only when there is no fp.
findings.scenario: At base, `.specclaw/changes/001-a/follow-ups.md` has `- [minor B1] ... <!-- fp:abc class:law -->`. The range only runs `git mv .specclaw/changes/001-a .specclaw/changes/archive/001-a`. `release base HEAD` lists the item under the archive path as newly added, marks it BLOCK and exits 1, although the range added nothing.

findings.message: `release_gate.block_on` is still parsed twice: `block_on()` here and `Config.block_on` plus `parse_block` in review_core.py. The parity test covers seven forms but not a compact sequence at the key's indent (`block_on:\n  - law`), where this parser stops because the item indent is not greater than the key indent. It also does not cover trailing comments. Add those forms to the parity table, or share one parser.

Both `post_review_status` copies capture `specclaw-review verdict --head` with `2>&1` and then take the round file from `sed -n 2p`. Any line the CLI writes to stderr, such as a config warning, shifts that line, and target_url points at the wrong path. The same applies in `plugins/specclaw-sync/bin/specclaw-azdo-pr`. Capture stdout only, and keep stderr for the 'not posted' message.

For a PR from a fork, `github.token` is read-only, so the `gh api .../statuses` call fails the job instead of emitting a notice. `target_url` also uses `$HEAD_REF` against the base repo, a branch that only exists in the fork, so the link 404s. Guard the step on `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, or link by SHA.
